draft.title: The polymerase chain reaction
card: PCR makes millions of copies of a chosen section of DNA from a very small sample. It is done in a machine that repeats a cycle of three steps.
the mixture is heated to about 95 °C. The hydrogen bonds between the two strands break, so the DNA becomes single strands.
the mixture is cooled. Short primers bind to the single strands at the start of the target section.
the mixture is warmed to about 72 °C. A heat-stable DNA polymerase adds nucleotides to each primer and builds new strands. Each cycle doubles the number of copies.
draft.remember: Heat to separate, cool to attach primers, warm to build. Each cycle doubles the DNA.

a.q: What happens to the DNA in the denaturing step of PCR?
opts: The two strands separate as hydrogen bonds break
Primers attach to the start of the target section
Polymerase adds nucleotides to build new strands
The DNA is cut into fragments of different sizes
a.why: Heating breaks the hydrogen bonds between the strands, leaving single strands. Primers attach in the annealing step, and building new strands is the extending step.
a.clue: Think about what high heat does to the bonds between strands.

b.q: A forensic lab starts a PCR with one copy of a target section. Assuming every cycle works fully, about how many copies exist after 5 cycles?
b.why: Each cycle doubles the number of copies, so 5 cycles gives 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32. Adding 5 copies per cycle would give a much smaller number, because copying is doubling, not adding.

a.best: The two strands separate as hydrogen bonds break

check.summary: No problems found. The card's temperatures and steps are accurate for VCE, and both questions have one clear answer (strands separate on denaturing; 2^5 = 32 copies).
